cta: NRG Bloom is building around modular speed because speed changes both economics and control.

scenes.text: If your African data-center plan takes two years to prove, you probably do not have an African data-center plan.
A two-year data-center timeline is not just slow in frontier markets. It is often structurally wrong.
A modular deployment can prove value before a conventional project would even finish its permitting deck.
Portable infrastructure changes negotiating leverage because the asset is not trapped to one site on day one.
In emerging-market infrastructure, speed compounds into trust, proof, and better capital efficiency.
The future of frontier compute will be built by teams that think like expeditionary infrastructure companies, not suburban real-estate developers.
Modular speed is not cosmetic. It is the difference between momentum and drift.

title: Speed Is Not a Feature in African Compute. It Is a Survival Trait.
